steps.name: Anxious Child
steps.text: Deedee, where are you?

steps.name: Anxious Child
steps.text: Look, I've brought your favorite jerky!
Eric! I found him!

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Where at, Miss Grani?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Whooooa! I can't get a hold of him, and he's gonna get away! Hurry!

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: C'mon now, this way. I have your jerky right over here, so stop running around.

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Where'd you find him, Miss Grani?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Phew, he was trying to make his way down into the sewers. But thanks to that shiny little rump, I was able to catch him before he could squirm down there.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But you've got to keep an eye on him, Eric. I'm not with the Mounted Police anymore, so I'm not gonna be able to help you find him on patrol anymore.

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Thanks, Miss Grani. And, I know... But it sure is weird. Deedee's usually so well-behaved, and never goes running around like this. Why'd he be trying to hide in the sewers?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Good question. You hear that, Deedee? Care to explain?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Huh? Did you get something dirty on you? It's all dark and... Hey! Don't climb on me!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Shoot, almost forgot! I need to head over to the hospital!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Sorry I'm late. Ran into a little incident while passing through the Infected district.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: More of your good deeds, Grani?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Heheh... So where's Kurt Jr.? He still with you guys?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Second bed on the right. Oh, but...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Thanks a bunch! I'll go pay him a visit!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Uhh...
He's not going to be able to answer any questions. The doctor has already administered his injection, and he just fell asleep.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Sir... How's your son doing right now?

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: The doctor said his condition was stable, but he keeps waking up in the middle of the night.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: Sometimes he starts screaming the moment he does. He'll grip my hands hard and cry, 'it hurts, dad!' But there's nothing I can do except wait for the doctor to rush over with the shot.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: More often than not, though, he just sits in bed staring at me without saying anything. As if those two wide eyes are looking right through me.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The doctors at Rhodes Island are very experienced in dealing with Oripathy. He WILL get better, it's just a matter of time.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Don't you worry. Even if the Mounted Police are no more, I'll get to the bottom of this case. Justice will be done!

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: You're a good officer, Grani. Always have been.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Grani, here's that Originium detector you wanted to borrow. It's a bit heavy though. You sure you can carry it back by yourself?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: No problem! Thanks, and sorry for imposing on you again.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Don't mention it. We've known each other long enough.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: By the way, is Kurt Jr.'s case not settled yet? Did the factory not provide any compensation?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Yeah. Before the Mounted Police were disbanded, we searched that factory from top to bottom for anything suspicious.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The eyewitness says he got caught up in the explosion in the distillation tower, which gave him Oripathy.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But there were no traces of an explosion or any contaminants in Work Area #3, where it allegedly happened. No sign of a cleanup either.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: That makes no sense.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Originally, the factory supervisor denied any sort of incident happened at all. Then later, they claimed that the Mounted Police failed to produce any evidence, and put pressure on the department to get our investigation shut down.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: And now that the Mounted Police are gone, the case has been transferred to the guards, and no way are they gonna do anything about it.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'That's an internal matter for Bolton Chemicals–' That's all the captain will say, in that pinched voice of his.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Kurt Jr. has been in that hospital bed for how long now? And they're still hanging up the investigation? Unbelievable.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Which is why it's up to me to keep things going.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But you're a guard in name only now, while they figure out where to reassign you. And even if you have the equipment to investigate, how are you going to get access to the factory?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: No one said it would be easy.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I can't even begin to imagine how hard it'll be.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Eh, don't worry about me. Heck, I've been a mountie long enough to make connections. I'll make sure things work out.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Oh, right. About Kurt Jr.... How's his condition, for real? I don't think you're giving his dad the whole truth.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: *sigh*... Nothing gets past you, does it? I didn't lie to him. I just... omitted the most harrowing detail.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: His condition has indeed stabilized, but his Cell-Originium Assimilation rate is very high. Coupled with the damage to his body caused by long-term physical labor, it's... hard to give a prognosis.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Even in the best case scenario, he may end up spending the rest of his life bedridden.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: He's only twenty-six years old, isn't he? No wonder you didn't want to break the news to his dad...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I promise you, Grani, we'll do everything we can.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I know, I trust you guys. Thanks, though.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Alright then, I'm gonna head back first. After I get this whole thing under wraps, let's hang out again!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: One sec.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: In addition to treating Oripathy, we're also very experienced at handling Originium contamination. If you ever need help with that, give us a call.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Got it. As a member of the Mounted– I mean, who do you think I am? Grani, that's who.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Two glasses of Big Johann's Special... Err, make that one special and one dry martini please. Appreciate it.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Phew–– Now then...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Here, over here!
Didn't expect us to be meeting up in a conspicuous place like this, Officer... I mean, Grani.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: It's the same place as always. Nothing wrong with that, is there?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Do you know how dangerous it is for me to meet with you privately these day?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Yeah, yeah. I'll make it up to you with this. Here, your favorite dry martini.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: So did you bring what I asked for?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Here you go. A list of all the orders Bolton Chemicals has made this past year.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Want me to start with the conclusion?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Go for it.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: You were right on the money. This last year, they've been ramping up their purchases of refined Originium, processing equipment, and raw materials. It's clear that they're upping production capacity.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: When it was already close to saturation? But why?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Londinium hasn't known peace for quite some time. Anyone with a keen eye can tell that our precious dukes have been getting jittery.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: High-speed battleships need maintenance, and armies need supplies. What better time to ramp up production for the days ahead?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Bolton Chemicals is the pillar of Rydell City’s industries. If they wanted to ramp up production, they could just go through the city...

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: But that takes money, which cuts into their bottom line. The most cost-effective way of increasing production capacity is... simply to have more in the first place.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Seeing how new contamination treatment equipment isn't anywhere on this list, they must still be using the same old equipment and pipelines that were already getting overwhelmed before.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: And the end result is... kaboom.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Thanks, I seriously owe you one. I can guarantee you this document's gonna come in handy. As for what comes next, I might need your help again.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Grani.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Huh? Yeah?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: I can't help you anymore.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Huh? Don't joke around like that. We've been working together for so long, and you know how much I rely on you.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: How about this? When we wrap up this Kurt Jr. case, I'll treat you to a nice meal at Rollin' Rotunda to show my appreciation. How does that sound?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: I'm serious, Grani. You're no longer Mounted Police, which means our cooperation has come to an end.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Moreover, as you've seen, this incident can't be boiled down to something as simple as 'a little accident happened and the factory refused to pay compensation.' It involves the future of a large enterprise. There's no need for you to wade into these murky waters.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Danny, don't try to talk me out of it.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: I'm not. It's just a warning. I'm saying this as your friend– don't pursue this case. It'll all resolve itself, which is in everyone's best interest anyway.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...Alright, if you want out, I'm not gonna stop you. I know you have your reasons, but I have mine too.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: This was the last case before the Mounted Police were disbanded. But we've seen our fair share, and it's not like we've never butted heads with Bolton Chemicals before either.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Plus, I can't just watch Kurt Jr. lie in bed for the rest of his life. It's my responsibility to keep investigating.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: There's that sense of justice again. This isn't some exam at the police academy. After all these years, do you still not understand the kind of land you live in?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Do you expect Bolton to just defer to you officers like before, bowing their heads and offering up a settlement to apologize? You've never seen them bare their fangs, have you?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I don't care; I'm not afraid of them. Do they have what it takes to stop the business end of my spear?

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: You think they'd only go after you? Hah. They've already made their move.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Notice how many people's eyes have been on you, ever since I stepped into this bar?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The folks who come to Big Johann's are all neighbors and fellow workers. I used to come here all the time after patrol, so I know them well.

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: Take a look at this then, Grani.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: What's this form?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'Notice: Due to ongoing investigations by the Mounted Police, the Rydell City factory has sustained significant economic losses. As such, management has unanimously decided that...'

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'Employee salaries and labor pensions will be reduced by percentage, according to the employee's rank. See the following table for details...'

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: What?! How dare they?!

steps.name: Mysterious Informant
steps.text: So, did you not notice... how quiet it's been in here?
Grani suddenly lifts her head. When she senses the gazes fixed on her from all directions, she feels like a fowlbeast perched alone on an empty branch.
Her surroundings are deathly quiet. Even their eyes are full of empty silence, like the wilderness itself.
Her throat starts to feel tight.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Hey there, guys...
A rock lands on the table with a heavy thud, knocking over the full glass of Big Johann's Special.
It's clear that it came from the street outside, shattering the glass and sailing over her head in a dangerous arc before landing front of her.
Grani sprints out of the bar.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Who did that?! Show yourself!
Her voice echoes through the night streets.
Not a soul is there to answer her.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Sorry for calling everyone here even though the Mounted Police have already been disbanded.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: You all remember the case with Kurt Jr., right? Well... I got my hands on new evidence confirming that Bolton Chemicals increased production capacity and created new work hazards in violation of safety regulations.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But I still don't have conclusive evidence proving that the explosion did in fact take place, meaning I don't have anything to submit to the relevant departments to force Bolton to admit fault for his injuries.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: A number of you... should be with the guards by now, so I'd like to ask for your help.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I borrowed a high-precision Originium detector in case I could find a way of getting back into the factory to do some investigating.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...So is anyone on board?

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: Chief...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I'm not your chief anymore. Just call me Grani.

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: Grani... It's way too dangerous to be investigating Bolton right now.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I know, I know. You've just taken your new posts, and you'd have to get your hands dirty for this. You might even take some heat for it.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But... Kurt Jr.'s situation isn't looking very good, and they're still putting more pressure on their other workers. This is urgent.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Do you still remember? The day we left the Mounted Police, we were all so upset that we couldn't scrounge up any evidence to keep this case alive. But now we have!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Maybe I don't even have to go in myself. If any of you can come up with a reason to take a look around and find some evidence, that's more than enough.

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: Grani, we...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: And after Kurt Jr. recovers, we can all go for some apple pie together. How nice would that be?

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: Chief, I'll give it to you straight. The captain warned all of us former mounties that we are strictly prohibited from pursuing any further investigations relating to Bolton.

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: In particular... we were forbidden from having any contact with you.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: What the...?

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: We're all taking a big risk just to meet like this, because we know the captain's a huge douche, and you're... always gonna be our chief.

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: Always have been, always will.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Lily... You guys...

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: Chief, I miss fighting alongside you, really. All we had to do was follow the shorty and charge forward without thinking. And somehow, everything would work itself out.

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: But since I left the Mounted Police, I came to a realization– outside of endlessly fighting and solving other people's problems, I also have a life of my own.

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: ...So I'm sorry, Chief.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: C'mon, don't give up. There has to be a way... We can talk it through, just like how we used to. Am I wrong?

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: Chief, Bolton controls the fate of so many people, including our neighbors, relatives, and loved ones.

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: They're serious this time. Even if we still wore our old uniforms, there'd be nothing we could do in the face of such a behemoth, let alone...

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: Just forget about the case already, Chief!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: All the more reason we can't stop now! If we don't make a stand, who will? Who's going to protect the next person to get hurt?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Listen up, you guys–

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: Grani! Have you never wondered why our city's Mounted Police was first to get disbanded?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Wasn't it just a reassignment–– Oh...

steps.name: Guards Member B
steps.text: There was nothing we could do back then, and there's nothing we can do now. Protecting others and stuff? Leave it to the powerful. It's not our job.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...I see, I get it now. Sorry, guys. I'm the one who should be apologizing. Don't let me keep you, then. I'll figure something out myself.

steps.name: Guards Member A
steps.text: Chief, there's still room in the Toron Guards. I'll put in a good word for you.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Thanks. But... you know how I am.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Can there really be no clues in all these investigation files?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Think Grani, think.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: No evidence of contaminant leakage was found in the factory, which means they must've had some way of moving it out.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Of course! They moved it out!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: If I can find evidence that they left traces of contaminants in the nearby environment, we can submit that to the Department of Oripathy Prevention and Control and request that they shut down the factory! And they absolutely can't afford to lose the factory!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Which means they'll have no choice but to admit fault while downplaying the issue and promising to improve their contamination treatment system.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But the question is, HOW did they manage to transport the contaminants?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I can't contact my informant anymore, can't get inside the factory, and can't go walking around the city waving an Originium detector around, so... what other options do I have...?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: *sigh* Guess I'll start at the outskirts of town and get familiar with the equipment first... Rhodes Island's stuff sure is high-tech, though. I think this is how you turn it on?

steps.name: System Voice
steps.text: Beep. Active Originium particles detected. Risk: Low...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Huh? In my room?!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: (Picks up the detection probe)

steps.name: System Voice
steps.text: Beep– Originium particle concentration increasing.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Is this... the mud I got on my clothes when I was searching for Deedee?!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: No way, don't tell me...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The domestic drainage pipes...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: We've been going at it all wrong from the start. We assumed they secretly treated the contaminants before transporting them away, but if they never bothered to treat them in the first place...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: They discharged contaminants directly into the pipelines of the Infected communities! Even if an outbreak took place, it'd just be blamed on the Infected!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Those bastards! How dare they stoop this low!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The black mud from before is gone, and the readings are back to normal... I guess they went and cleaned it up.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: But... when we inspected the discharge facilities in Work Area #3, we found no signs of pipes being replaced.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Well, I'll worry about that later! Now that I know what they were doing, I'll find the evidence as long as I keep digging. This'll prevent it from spreading to the Infected communities, too!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Or... maybe I could ask Rhodes Island for help.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Huh? Lily? At this hour...?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Hello? Is something wrong?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The case is about to be closed? Kurt Sr. agreed to sign a Letter of Understanding?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: At the factory? I'll be there right away!

steps.name: Factory Security
steps.text: Hey, you! Hold up, you're not allowed inside!

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Out of the way!

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Is that the former Mounted Police officer from before? Let her in.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Good day, Miss Grani... Former Mounted Police.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: The agreement was signed by both parties, and handled without issue by the guards. Of course, we do appreciate the Mounted Police's previous cooperation on this matter.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: ...Don't care to shake hands? So be it.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: You... Do you have any idea what you've done?

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Calm down, ma'am. I'm just doing what I'm paid for, so don't take it out on me.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Go back and tell your boss this: I've found evidence that the factory has been leaking contaminants and dumping them into domestic pipelines! And they're not gonna get away with it!

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: I'll pass it on verbatim. However... as it stands, the case is legally closed.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Out of respect for you, I must remind you that you are no longer a Mounted Police officer. With no one to back you up, waving a weapon around like that is most disgraceful.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Whatever you think you're about to do, you may find it difficult to retain legal assistance in the matter.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...They should just surrender themselves! They'll be brought to justice for their arrogance!

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Thank you for your contribution to Rydell City. I sincerely hope that you have a long and successful career ahead of you.

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: Also, in your future endeavors, please double check that the work area number wasn't changed.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Retained Lawyer
steps.text: I'll be taking my leave. Oh right, Kurt Sr., the compensation funds will be transferred to your account shortly. Please take a look.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Why, sir?! We were so close to getting justice for your son! You didn't have to sign off on this!

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: ...Grani, you're a good kid, and you've always been a good officer.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: But... you're not one of Rydell City's laborers. I've worked here my entire life, and the same goes for my son.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: And I can help you both! Please believe me! I'm not gonna give up on this!

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: My son, he... he's already gone.
Grani can only stand there blankly.
She walks down the street, alone.
She takes one deep breath after another, letting the murky, industrial air fill her lungs.
She unclenches her fist, her knuckles now white, and gently pats her spear case slung over her shoulder.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...It's just you and me now.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Let's go grab a bite first. If we keep at it, there might just be a way.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: This is nothing I can't handle myself...
A gust of wind blows past, lifting a stack of waste paper beside a trash can.
She grabs hold of a page from a fluttering newspaper and sees something printed inconspicuously at the bottom.
She holds her breath.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'A car accident... on Third Avenue...'

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'Bolton Chemicals manager Danny Coleman was critically injured and sent to the hospital for treatment, where he remains unconscious...'
She crumples the piece of paper into a tiny wad, her thin body trembling slightly.
She stops walking and turns her eyes upward, only to see dark clouds gathering in the sky.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Oh...
*sobbing*––

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Someone's crying? Where's it coming from...?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Eric?

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: *sniffle*... *sob*...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: What's wrong, Eric? What happened?

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Miss Grani... It's Deedee... He...

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: After we found him that day, he stopped moving and refused to eat...
She sees the beastling curled up in the boy's arms like a newborn.
Its paw trembles, and after a violent spasm, it collapses like a deflated balloon.
Its breathing stops.

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Deedee? Deedee? What's the matter with you? Deedee?
Grani squeezes the beastling's still-warm paw.
Just as she had expected, she notices a hard, grainy feeling against her fingertips.
The crystal particles that broke through its skin have claimed yet another life.

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: No, this can't be happening! Why Deedee? He was always so nice and well-behaved, never bit anyone, was never bad...

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: Right? He was always good, right Miss Grani?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Eric...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Deedee has gone somewhere far away. A kinder, more beautiful place.

steps.name: Eric
steps.text: No... Why did it have to be Deedee...?
The child lets out a sob and tightly clings to the beastling's body.
She hugs the child close.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: That's right... It never should've happened to Kurt Jr., or to Deedee. It shouldn't have been them.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: ...Hello? This is Grani.
Five days later.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: My son...

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Sir...

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: Grani... Didn't you already leave?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I brought flowers for Kurt Jr.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Do you miss him?

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: ...When he was still around, we used to fight all the time. I cussed him out in the most vicious ways, and kicked him out of the house.

steps.name: Kurt Sr.
steps.text: But recently, I've been seeing him in my dreams. He'd follow me calling 'daddy, daddy,' just like when he was little.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Did you dream about him on the day you signed that Letter of Understanding?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: In my dream, I saw him, all the other Mounted Police, and all of Rydell City's neighbors and workers holding hands and going round-and-round in a big circle for his twenty-seventh birthday.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: The candlelight shone on his face. He was singing and dancing with such a joyous expression.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Sir, I left five days ago to reach out to a certain company.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: And now I'm back to keep my promise.
Only then does the old man realize that the youth beside him is clutching a cold, glimmering spear in her other hand.
She grips its shaft resolutely.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I hate those who misbehave, those who bully the weak, and those who would manipulate our lives as they please.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I promise you– as long as I can hold this spear, I will do everything in my power to see those people pay.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: And I never go back on my word.
